analysis.title: Valero Energy Corp. (VLO): Takeaways from Management Meetings: Low Cost Operator, Returning Capital and With Gulf Coast Advantage
key_insights: GS reiterates Buy on VLO with a $496 6-month price target, based on 14.0x P/E on normalized EPS and SOTP. Price was $334.18 on 20 Nov 2026, implying 48.4% upside.
VLO shares are +105% in 2026 vs S&P +1%, but are down 23% in the last month vs S&P down 10%. GS calls the consolidation an attractive entry point.

Gulf Coast crude differentials remain favorable. The basket (WTI Houston, Maya, WCS Houston, ASCI) is at a $15/b discount to Brent this quarter vs a 4-year average of $7/b, and spot is closer to $13/b.

Management expects supply growth from Canada and Latin America, which could pressure heavy differentials. Strait oil volumes have improved toward pre-war levels, and freight costs have eased but Valero stays biased higher on freight vs spot.

VLO has near $10B of cash, well above the $4-5B long-term guidance. GS expects at least 50% of cash flow from operations returned to shareholders, with cash still building into year-end and the share count shrinking.

Spot gasoline margin weakness is attributed to butane blending under winter grade specs and high utilization from deferred turnarounds. Valero sees no meaningful demand destruction in the US or Canada wholesale system.

About 1.5 million b/d of global refining turnarounds were deferred per the latest earnings call. Valero sees gasoline as attractive into next Spring as turnarounds pick up and the industry maximizes distillate.
The Houston refinery acquisition from LYB is expected to earn at least a 25% after-tax IRR at forward mid-cycle pricing with minimal commercial synergies. Spending stays within the $2.0-2.5B budget.

The LYB Houston asset brings 165,000 b/d of light sweet capacity, about 700 acres on the Ship Channel, 13.5 mn bbls of storage, and marine, rail and truck logistics. It offers upside from future heavy sour processing investment and lower system cash opex per bbl.
GS forecasts VLO EPS of $60.23 for 12/26E, $49.38 for 12/27E and $28.62 for 12/28E, versus $10.65 for 12/25. Key risks are refining margins, operational execution and capital returns.

market_movers.rationale: Post-meeting pullback creates entry point. Strong Gulf Coast crude discounts, heavy capital return and accretive Houston refinery deal support the target.

sector_views.rationale: Forward margins remain strong, with deferred turnarounds and distillate incentives supporting the setup into Spring.

earnings_insights: GS estimates VLO EPS of $60.23 for FY 12/26E, $49.38 for FY 12/27E and $28.62 for FY 12/28E, vs $10.65 reported for 12/25.
GS quarterly EPS: $23.90 for 9/26 (shown as actual period), $19.56 est for 12/26E, $13.53 est for 3/27E, $13.75 est for 6/27E.
GS estimates FCF yield of 16.5% for 2026E and 13.9% for 2027E.
